pr_title: Feature: Added support for Infomaniak kDrive
pr_body:
**Resolved / Related Issues**

To prevent extra work, all changes to the Files codebase must link to an approved issue marked as `Ready to build`. Please insert the issue number following the hashtag with the issue number that this Pull Request resolves.
- Closes #15475

**Steps used to test these changes**

Stability is a top priority for Files and all changes are required to go through testing before being merged into the repo. Please include a list of steps that you used to test this PR.

1. kDrive is displayed in Files and copying of files etc. is possible


Note: The Sync Status column is not displayed, but this does not work in Windows File Explorer either. I think kDrive does not set the property [“System.FilePlaceholderStatus”](https://github.com/files-community/Files/blob/main/src/Files.App/ViewModels/ShellViewModel.cs#L1885) correctly, which Files (and probably also Windows File Explorer) uses to find out the status.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/604f4c10-8ff5-4fed-bc60-68712e95c9fc)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddab11d6-45f8-42d4-a7dc-5dbd6570842f)
pr_comments: @mafra99 does this still work if the user changes the location from kDrive settings?

I have just reinstalled kDrive and now the entry in the registry no longer contains an application name, but only an ID. As a result, kDrive is no longer recognized on my device.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfec69f3-1846-4029-907c-d68637e48c74)


I can think of two other ways to recognize kDrive anyway: 
1. Using the DefaultIcon under Computer\HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\CLSID\<>\DefaultIcon to check whether the path contains kDrive
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8276b42-329e-4293-a198-01f8b7199032)

2. Via the entry in Computer\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\SyncRootManager
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7c64c1f-565c-4c05-aadd-1cd5825e1344)

To use the entry from SyncRootManager seems safer to me, I have pushed a commit that contains the changes for this.


In the second commit I cleaned up the code a bit and fixed a few warnings.

The method GetDriveType is new and returns the drive type, e.g. iCloudDrive or kDrive. This should make the method DetectGenericCloudDrive a little simpler.
Compared to before, the DriveType is now returned directly as soon as one is detected and the checks for the other DriveTypes are no longer executed.

> @mafra99 does this still work if the user changes the location from kDrive settings?

@yaira2 thanks, that actually didn't work. should also be fixed

issue_context.title: Feature: Add support for Infomaniak kDrive cloud
issue_context.body:
### What feature or improvement do you think would benefit Files?

kDrive ([https://www.infomaniak.com/kdrive](https://www.infomaniak.com/kdrive)) doesn't show up in the cloud section. The folder is usually located in the user profile folder.

### Requirements

- This proposal will make the kDrive folder appear in the cloud section in sidebar
- The standard cloud-specific operations and icons should be supported


### Files Version

3.4.1.0

### Windows Version

10.0.22621.3593

### Comments

_No response_
comments: Thanks for the feedback, I've added this to the project board.
This is now on our todo list

For our own reference
> Hello, Thanks for integrating kDrive into your product!
> 
> "we would verify the installation of kDrive" => You can use the following PowerShell command.
> 
> ```
> PS C:\Users\Chris> get-package -Name kDrive
> 
> Name                           Version          Source                           ProviderName
> ----                           -------          ------                           ------------
> kDrive                         3.6.0                                             Programs
> ```
> 
> "retrieve its path to display in the cloud drives segment of our sidebar" => Are you talking about the path of the app or the synchronized folders? The exe path is: C:\Program Files (x86)\kDrive\kDrive.exe
> 
> You can find the synchronised folders by browsing Windows Registry keys in "Computer\HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes\CLSID" and filter on "kDrive". The folder path is the value of the key "targetFolderPath" in "Computer\HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes\CLSID<clsid>\Instance\InitPropertyBag"
@manfromarce this feature will be included in our next release.
